A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PALM and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably, including the additional appendix content in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–D report original simulation and real-robot evaluations, ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds a real-robot failure analysis in Appendix C.3 and Table 11.

M1.justification: The four affordance components, transformer architecture, diffusion action–progress decoder, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The new progress-label paragraph documents existing supervision without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training datasets, LIBERO suites, CALVIN ABC→D, and real-world tasks and perturbations are retained. Appendix C.3 analyzes the existing six-subtask robot task without establishing additional task or environmental coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding benchmark tables is unchanged. New Table 11 reuses OpenVLA and Octo, already the real-robot comparators in Table 5.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces a 50-rollout-per-method analysis with episode-level repeat, skip, and premature-stop rates, counting episodes with at least one event under common detection rules. The existing 20-rollout real-world evaluation and simulation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 11 quantify whether PALM reduces repeated motions, skipped subtasks, and premature stopping. Existing component, data-source, threshold, prediction-target, and perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: LIBERO retains standard errors across three seeds with 500 episodes each. Table 11 adds an episode sample size and failure rates, but no new seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing reported results are unchanged. New Table 11 reports average lengths of 2.30, 1.85, and 3.90 for OpenVLA, Octo, and PALM, respectively, and PALM repeat/skip/premature-stop rates of 14%/8%/10%. These are additional 50-rollout results, not revisions of Table 5.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–10 remain unchanged; neither version supplies theoretical proofs. The new failure-rate descriptions concern empirical evaluation metrics and introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same affordance-plus-progress contributions and headline claims: 91.8% LIBERO-LONG success, 12.5% CALVIN improvement, and strong real-world generalization. Conclusion edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix F acknowledges limited recovery under execution drift, occlusion, contact uncertainty, and deformation, plus annotation and processing overhead. It proposes recovery, reinforcement-learning, and 3D-perception directions. Appendix A.2 also adds an explanation of cross-domain progress-label consistency.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly describes manual functional-keyframe annotation, fixed semantic progress anchors, linear interpolation, and shared human-video/robot milestones. v2 also adds a project-page link. Existing hardware, architecture configurations, training hyperparameters, and rollout details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Cited coverage expands substantially across VLMs, progress learning, affordances, failure recovery, and 3D/world models, including GR00T N1, RoboBrain, Robo-Dopamine, RoboAfford++, SAFE, and PointWorld. References such as HyperTASR and PIVOT-R disappear. PALM's central positioning remains stable; bibliographic metadata updates alone are not counted.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include localized copyediting, explicit appendix cross-references, a shortened conclusion, the progress-label paragraph, and new subsections C.3 and F, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with rearranged inputs and revised colors and labels; Figure 1 receives label corrections. Table 11 is added, Figure 3 and several tables shift position, and tighter layout keeps the abstract on the first page. Existing result visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through progress-label construction details and specific recovery limitations, while Table 11 adds targeted evidence about the failures motivating PALM. The gains are limited: the core method and benchmark results are unchanged, and the new failure analysis lacks uncertainty estimates and precise detection thresholds.
